{{technical|date=April 2014}}
The '''frequency domain decomposition''' ('''FDD''') is an output-only [[system identification]] technique popular in [[civil engineering]], in particular in [[structural health monitoring]].  As an output-only algorithm, it is useful when the input data is unknown.  FDD is a [[modal analysis]] technique which generates a [[system realization]] using the frequency response given (multi-)output data.<ref name="OutputOnly">{{Cite journal | last1 = Brincker | first1 = R. | last2 = Zhang | first2 = L. | last3 = Andersen | first3 = P. | doi = 10.1088/0964-1726/10/3/303 | title = Modal identification of output-only systems using frequency domain decomposition | journal = Smart Materials and Structures | volume = 10 | issue = 3 | pages = 441 | year = 2001 | bibcode = 2001SMaS...10..441B | s2cid = 250917814 | url = http://vbn.aau.dk/ws/files/203990023/Modal_Identification_of_Output_Only_Systems_using_Frequency_Domain_Decomposition.pdf }}</ref><ref name="Ambient">{{cite conference|author=Brincker, R.|author2=Zhang, L.|author3=Andersen, P.|title=Modal Identification from Ambient Response Using Frequency Domain Decomposition|book-title=Proc. of the 18th International Modal Analysis Conference|location=San Antonio, TX|date=February 7–10, 2000|url=http://www.svibs.com/solutions/literature/2000_2.pdf|access-date=March 11, 2012}}</ref>

== Algorithm ==
# Estimate the [[power spectral density]] matrix <math>\hat{G}_{yy}(j\omega)</math> at discrete frequencies <math>\omega = \omega_i</math>.
# Do a [[singular value decomposition]] of the power spectral density, i.e. <math>\hat{G}_{yy}(j \omega_i) = U_i S_i U_i^H</math> where <math>U_i = [u_{i1},u_{i2},...,u_{im}]</math> is a [[unitary matrix]] holding the [[singular vector]]s <math>u_{ij}</math>, <math>S_i</math> is the diagonal matrix holding the singular values <math>s_{ij}</math>.
# For an <math>n</math> degree of freedom system, then pick the <math>n</math> dominating peaks in the power spectral density using whichever technique you wish (or manually).  These peaks correspond to the [[mode shape]]s.<ref name="OutputOnly"/>
## Using the mode shapes, an input-output system realization can be written.
